concept.name: Trading range
concept.definition: A relatively tight horizontal price band, bounded by support below and resistance above, within which prices move while supply and demand are roughly balanced. In classical chart analysis a break of either boundary is taken as evidence that one side has gained control — a heuristic, not a law.
concept.intuition: A tug-of-war zone: neither bulls nor bears can push price out of the box, until suddenly one side wins.
concept.mechanics: Marked by drawing horizontal lines or zones at the range's reaction highs (resistance) and reaction lows (support); ranges can persist for weeks to months. Resolution is read from a decisive break of a boundary, ideally confirmed by expanding volume.
concept.failure_modes: False breakouts at range boundaries are common; in wide or long-lived ranges the 'exact' levels are fuzzy enough that zone-based marking is more honest than single-price lines.
concept.misconceptions: That merely touching a range boundary is a tradable signal; without confirmation, boundary touches and marginal breaks fail frequently.
concept.example: ChartSchool documents WorldCom oscillating between support at 55 and resistance at 63 for about five months in 1999, including a false breakout above 62, before the range broke down through 55.
